title: SharePoint: FAQ web part becomes non-AI, with AI FAQ generation in Copilot in SharePoint
summary: The briefing passes: the authoring change, rollout facts, licensing background and site controls are supported by the supplied Microsoft records and the cited Learn pages. It correctly distinguishes the FAQ-specific documentation gaps and reports the disagreement over GCC availability.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level control, not a new FAQ-specific setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enabling Restricted Content Discovery removes Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions from the site.
claims.quote: If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: The UI route is SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: API and automation
claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: By default only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Management of Restricted Content Discovery can optionally be delegated to site administrators.
claims.quote: If you want site administrators to manage the setting for their own sites, enable delegation by using the following PowerShell command:

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organization to have a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery also has the prerequisites specified by its cited Learn page.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available. See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes AI entry points such as the Copilot button and Create pages with AI.
claims.quote: Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: Learn says the existing preview PowerShell availability settings remained in effect until November 1, 2026.
claims.quote: Existing PowerShell settings remain in effect until November 1, 2026.

claims.claim: Learn directs administrators to manage availability through Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery after November 1, 2026.
claims.quote: After November 1, 2026, manage availability by using Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this FAQ web part authoring change at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint FAQ web part authoring experience manually creating editing managing FAQs Copilot'; read Learn results and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. No Learn description of this FAQ change was returned; the opened page does not name FAQ generation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published an explicit classification of FAQ generation as everyday or advanced work.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot in SharePoint FAQ generation Copilot Credits rate licensing FAQ'; read results and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started, including its licensing table. The general everyday/advanced distinction is published, but FAQ generation is not named.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A Copilot Credits rate specific to FAQ generation is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot in SharePoint FAQ generation Copilot Credits rate licensing FAQ'; read the returned licensing and billing excerpts and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. No FAQ-generation-specific credit rate was found.

claims.claim: The roadmap and supplied notice describe manual FAQ authoring without a licence statement.
claims.quote: Searched: licence/license in the supplied roadmap description and full MC1476319 post, and Learn for 'SharePoint FAQ web part ... manual licensing'. Neither supplied record gives a manual-authoring licence statement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied Microsoft description does not specify which grounding sources authors can select.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint FAQ web part ... grounding sources'; read roadmap description, MC1476319, Learn results and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. The FAQ descriptions say 'selected grounding sources' without identifying selectable source types.

claims.claim: The supplied Microsoft description does not explain how FAQ grounding sources relate to author permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint FAQ web part ... permissions identity grounding sources'; read roadmap description, MC1476319, Learn results and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. No FAQ-specific relationship between source selection and author permissions was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's FAQ description does not state whether authors review generated content before saving or publishing it.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint FAQ web part ... review before save publish'; read roadmap description, MC1476319, Learn results and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. The FAQ descriptions state where content is saved, not whether an author reviews it first.

claims.claim: No new identity or permission model is described for the FAQ web part change.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint FAQ web part ... permissions identity'; read roadmap description, MC1476319, Learn results and copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. No new identity or permission model for this FAQ change was described.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, reflecting the documented Copilot in SharePoint hybrid model rather than asserting a FAQ-specific meter.
claims.quote: Copilot in SharePoint uses a hybrid business model. Everyday individual productivity is included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no admin setting specific to the FAQ web part authoring change at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint FAQ web part admin disable authoring setting PowerShell'; read Learn results, copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started and restricted-content-discovery. These describe general site AI controls, not an FAQ-authoring-specific admin setting.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery page does not describe its effects on the FAQ web part itself.
claims.quote: Searched: FAQ/web part in the fully opened restricted-content-discovery page, and Learn for 'SharePoint FAQ web part admin disable authoring setting PowerShell'. The cited page describes AI entry-point restrictions without naming the FAQ web part.
